mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in the unemployment rate above 8% signals weakening labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE crosses above 8%, or UNRATE remains above 8% without a subsequent negative return.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in economic demand (GDPC1) and consumer demand (HOUST) strengthen market confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of GDPC1 and HOUST does not lead to statistically significant positive 5-day returns (t-test p > 0.05) in at least 60% of instances where both proxies increase.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, rising demand (GDPC1) while falling supply (INDPRO) indicates potential market overvaluation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 5% and INDPRO decline > 2% in 3 months within late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, the predicted negative returns do not occur when GDPC1 rises >5% and INDPRO falls >2%, or the returns are not significantly negative (t-test p >0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate paired with rising economic demand (GDPC1) creates favorable conditions for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 move in tandem without a significant positive return in 20-day horizon, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and GDPC1 rise is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Sustained inflationary pressures (CPIAUCSL exceeding 3%) erode investor confidence, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3%, or the effect persists beyond the initial 2-month period without a sustained decline.

mechanism_narrative: Stronger supply growth (INDPRO) reflects robust production capacity, boosting market optimism and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not consistently correlate with positive 5-day S&P 500 returns over multiple cycles, or the correlation coefficient is below 0.2 over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery, falling unemployment (UNRATE <6%) alongside tight monetary policy (FEDFUNDS >1%) signals economic stabilization, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-shock recovery periods, the combination of UNRATE <6% and FEDFUNDS >1% does not lead to significantly positive 20-day returns (t-test p>0.05), or the effect is not observed in at least 70% of such regimes.
